subject: Anthropic IPO tests Europe’s AI boom
notes: The lead essay says Anthropic debuted yesterday; the podcast blurb in the same issue says it is about to start trading. The Plural fund appears twice (essay and fund list) and is one entry. Isomorphic Labs appears only as a headline link with no body text.

stories.headline: Anthropic lists on Nasdaq, raising about $81.3bn in the largest IPO in history
stories.quote: Raising about $81.3bn in its listing — the largest IPO in history — Anthropic popped in early trading amid big investor demand.

facts.text: Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq the day before the issue.
facts.quote: Over 4,000 miles away from New York’s Nasdaq stock exchange, seemingly everyone in Helsinki has been talking about Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO. The AI model maker officially debuted yesterday, giving the public market its first taste of a frontier AI startup.

facts.text: Raised about $81.3bn in the listing, described as the largest IPO in history; shares rose in early trading.
facts.quote: Raising about $81.3bn in its listing — the largest IPO in history — Anthropic popped in early trading amid big investor demand.

facts.text: Priced at $83 per share; reports put the valuation at $1.4tn before pricing. Menlo Ventures partner Deedy Das considers that probably too low.
facts.quote: Deedy Das, a partner at Menlo Ventures (one of Anthropic’s early and big backers), reckons a $1.4tn valuation, which reports put its valuation before it priced at $83 per share, is probably too low.

facts.text: The podcast blurb in the same issue describes Anthropic as about to start trading.
facts.quote: Anthropic is about to start trading in what is the market’s first test of a frontier AI lab going public.

stories.headline: Plural raises €1bn for its third fund
stories.quote: London- and Tallinn-based Plural raised €1bn for its third fund. The fund will focus on early-stage “non-obvious” companies .

facts.text: The fund is Plural's third and largest, and one of the biggest such vehicles in Europe.
facts.quote: Elsewhere in Europe, London- and Tallinn-based VC firm Plural announced a whopping €1bn fund, its third and largest, and one of the biggest such vehicles in Europe.

stories.headline: Sofinnova Partners raises €725m for its second crossover fund
stories.quote: Paris-based VC Sofinnova Partners raised €725m for its second crossover fund. The firm focuses on late-stage life sciences companies.

stories.headline: European hardware startups have raised €26.9bn in equity so far this year, 51% more than in all of 2025, per Sifted data
stories.quote: European startups developing hardware have raised €26.9bn in equity funding so far this year, 51% more than in the whole of 2025, according to Sifted data. That’s 38% of all VC money raised in Europe this year.

facts.text: Slush held its first exclusively hardware-focused event, the Hardware Foundry.
facts.quote: hardtech was on full display in the demo space of the Hardware Foundry — the mega startup conference Slush’s first exclusively hardware-focused event.

facts.text: Andreas Klinger of Prototype Capital called the current tech market a bubble.
facts.quote: “It's 100% a bubble,” he said of what's happening in the tech market right now.
